newsitem.title: UK: Sears chief prepares break-up plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sears chief prepares break-up plan - paper.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc is planning to announce the disposal of its ailing British Shoe Corporation (BSC) in two weeks' time, the Observer newspaper said on Sunday.
Sears is expected to announce profits 20 percent down on the 100 million pounds ($162.8 million) made in the year to January 31 1996 when it reports its results later this month.

The company was not immediately available for comment on the Observer report which said Sears chief executive Liam Strong wants to reshape the group into two divisions, the Selfridges department store plus its women's clothing shops.
The paper said Strong would present the plan to executive directors this week. It said analysts beleived the cost of shedding its shoe business could be "as little as 50 million pounds".
The Sunday Times said Strong was likely to step down once the break-up had been completed.
It said his plan was "thought to involve a restructuring that would unshackle Sears' more successful busineses from BSC".

The Sunday Telegraph said that Sir Bob Reid, chairman of the group, was considering putting himself up for re-election at the annual meeting in June to end what he calls "a whispering campaign" against the group.
The paper said Reid was responding to suggestions that he and Strong were about to be axed in a board room coup by non-executive directors of the group.
It quoted Reid as saying there was a "deliberate destabilisation campaign by people who want to get Sears assets on the cheap". He was "determined to prevent this", the Sunday Telegraph added.
